title: fix(metadata-protocol): an update by id answers the same refusal whether or not the id exists, as delete does
body:
domain:devx#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcVy4VXmkQjn2MGeaWk

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no file under `skills/**` teaches what a by-id update answers for an id that names no record (a `git grep` of `skills/` for `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` names only the approvals record lock), so no skill line changes. The Update Record section of `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx` states the order.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:按 id 更新记录时,先判断"这次更新允不允许",再查"记录在不在"——与按 id 删除的顺序一致。覆盖单条 `PATCH`、批量 `updateMany`、`batch`(update)三个入口,以及经它们更新的所有入口(dispatcher `/data`、`/mcp` HTTP 工具、声明式更新动作)。
- **为什么改**:QA 第三轮发现的安全加固(细节按披露裁决不公开)
- **风险与回滚**:不允许更新该对象的调用方(无编辑权限,或外部数据源只读)对不存在的 id 现在收到与存在的 id 相同的 403,原来是 404;有权限的调用方、成功更新、`405`、乐观锁(`If-Match`)、upsert 与系统上下文写入均不变。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:① `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` 的 `updateData`——删掉写前的存在性探测,改为引擎返回 `null` 后再查存在;② `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-batch-data.ts` 的两处 update 分支(同一改法);③ `packages/qa/dogfood/test/update-by-id-refusal-order.dogfood.test.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/update-by-id-refusal-order.dogfood.test.ts` —— 预期 16/16 通过(四类对象上 PATCH、批量更新、DELETE 对"存在/不存在"的 id 给出同一个回答,另有编辑权限、行级范围、管理员三组对照)。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

An update by id now answers the same refusal whether or not the id exists, as delete does.

- **`updateData`** (`PATCH /api/v1/data/:object/:id`, and every door that updates through it: the runtime dispatcher's `/data`, the `/mcp` HTTP tools, `callData`, declarative update actions) no longer reads the record before calling `engine.update`. The engine judges the write first — the security middleware's object- and row-level verdicts, the external datasource's write guard — and then its own by-id not-found gate (inside the middleware chain, ahead of every `before*` hook) answers `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` to a caller the write is open to. The protocol asks existence (the system-context probe) only when the engine resolved a `null` readback: that keeps the `404` for an engine that resolves `null` for a missing row, and keeps `200 { record: null }` for an update that moved its row out of the caller's row scope.
- **Optimistic concurrency** on `updateData` is asked the way `deleteData` asks it: `assertVersionMatch`, a probe only when the caller sent a token.
- **`updateManyData` and `batchData`'s `update` operation**: the same — no probe ahead of the engine, the existence check after a `null` readback, per row.
- **Docs**: the Update Record section of `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx` states the order.

Unchanged, and already one answer for both ids for a caller refused the operation: `DELETE` on every door and the cross-object `POST /api/v1/batch` (the engine judges first), and clone and the record field-access read, which load the record through the read door first (each measured at the HTTP door on the stock showcase). The action-by-id record load, the MCP stdio bridge's `update_record` / `delete_record` and `callData`'s no-protocol fallback likewise read the record as the caller, through the read door, before any write, on their update and delete arms alike (read in code).

## Tests

- **HTTP door (dogfood, stock showcase)** — `packages/qa/dogfood/test/update-by-id-refusal-order.dogfood.test.ts`, 16 cases. A plain member (baseline only) on `showcase_project_membership`, `sys_user_permission_set`, `showcase_ext_customer` and `showcase_ext_order`: `PATCH`, `updateMany` and `batch` (update) answer the same status and body for an id that names a row and one that names none; `DELETE` keeps its one answer; a stale `If-Match` keeps one status and code. Controls: a member holding the edit grant updates (200) and gets `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` for no row; a member with edit and a row-level restriction (`showcase_private_note`) gets one not-found answer for a foreign row and for no row and still updates its own; the administrator updates (200), gets `404` for no row on an ordinary object, and gets `EXTERNAL_WRITE_FORBIDDEN` for both ids on a read-only federated object, as its `DELETE` does; refused writes leave the row untouched.
- **Engine** — `packages/objectql/src/engine-write-not-found-gate.test.ts` gains section 5: a refusal the middleware chain answers comes before the by-id not-found gate, for update and delete, and nothing reaches the driver.
- **Protocol** — `protocol.record-not-found.test.ts`: a refused write answers the same for a real and a missing id on `updateData` and `deleteData` with no read ahead of the engine; the post-write existence check is asked as the system and keeps the `200` of an update that moved its row out of scope. `protocol.bulk-record-not-found.test.ts`: the same parity on `updateManyData` and `batchData`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Fixture triage.** The bulk and batch-conformance doubles answered a missing id with an unclassified throw (the write pipeline's old answer); they now refuse it the way ObjectQL's by-id gate does — after the write is judged, before any hook — and "the write pipeline never ran for that row" is asserted on a `pipeline` spy instead of "the engine was never called". The engine-layer guarantee is pinned by the engine's own not-found gate tests. `update-path-id-wins` and two runtime tests change their read counts: a tokenless `PATCH`, like a tokenless `DELETE`, reads nothing ahead of the engine, and a refused `PATCH` on a plugin driver costs the remote no read.
- **Admin on a read-only federated object.** An unknown id now answers the write guard's `403 EXTERNAL_WRITE_FORBIDDEN`, the answer its `DELETE` already gave, where it answered `404`.
